title: Public nuisance
old_text: An act or illegal omission causing common injury, danger or annoyance to the public or people in the vicinity.
new_text: Defines public nuisance as an act or illegal omission causing common injury, danger or annoyance to the public.
punishment_old: Defined only; punishment provided in Section 290 (fine up to Rs. 200)
punishment_new: Defined provision; general punishment provided in Section 297 (fine up to Rs. 1,000)
explanation: BNS Section 270 replaces IPC Section 268 defining public nuisance without substantial alteration of core elements. It covers acts or omissions causing common injury, danger, or annoyance to the public. General punishment is linked to Section 297.

title: Negligent act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life
old_text: Unlawfully or negligently doing an act known to be likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life.
new_text: Unlawfully or negligently doing an act known to be likely to spread infection of infectious disease dangerous to life.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 271 replaces IPC Section 269 for negligent transmission of life-threatening infectious disease. The provision modernizes epidemic control enforcement while retaining the six-month penalty ceiling. Fines have been revised to contemporary standards.

title: Malignant act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life
old_text: Malignantly doing any act known to be likely to spread the infection of any disease dangerous to life.
new_text: Malignantly doing an act known to be likely to spread infection of any disease dangerous to life.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 272 corresponds to IPC Section 270 covering deliberate and malicious propagation of dangerous disease. The mens rea requires malice rather than mere negligence, attracting heavier imprisonment up to 2 years.

title: Disobedience to quarantine rule
old_text: Knowingly disobeying quarantine rules established by government for vessels or places of infection.
new_text: Knowingly disobeying quarantine regulations or isolation rules established by government.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 273 replaces IPC Section 271 punishing breach of official quarantine and isolation orders. The provision penalizes willful disregard of epidemic containment protocols established by public authorities.

title: Adulteration of food or drink intended for sale
old_text: Adulterating food or drink so as to make it noxious, intending or knowing it will be sold as food or drink.
new_text: Adulterating any article of food or drink to make it noxious, intending to sell or knowing it is likely to be sold.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 274 penalizes making food or drink noxious by adulteration for commercial sale, replacing IPC Section 272. The monetary fine ceiling has been elevated to reflect modern economic standards.

title: Sale of noxious food or drink
old_text: Selling or offering or exposing for sale noxious food or drink knowing or having reason to believe it is noxious.
new_text: Selling, offering or exposing for sale any food or drink known or believed to be unfit or noxious.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 275 replaces IPC Section 273 punishing vendors who market noxious or spoiled food and beverage. It enforces food safety standards alongside consumer protection statutes.

title: Adulteration of drugs
old_text: Adulterating drugs or medical preparations so as to lessen their efficacy, change their operation, or make them noxious.
new_text: Adulterating any drug or medical preparation to reduce efficacy, alter operation, or make it noxious.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 276 replaces IPC Section 274 for adulterating medicinal drugs and pharmaceutical preparations. The maximum term of imprisonment has been enhanced to 1 year to deter counterfeit and spurious pharmaceuticals.

title: Sale of adulterated drugs
old_text: Knowingly selling, offering, or issuing adulterated drugs for medicinal use.
new_text: Knowingly selling, exposing, issuing or distributing adulterated drugs for medicinal use.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 277 replaces IPC Section 275 penalizing the commercial dispensing or sale of adulterated medicines. The enhanced punishment of up to 1 year imprisonment reinforces stricter medicine distribution controls.

title: Sale of drug as a different drug or preparation
old_text: Knowingly selling, offering or issuing any drug or medical preparation as a different drug or preparation.
new_text: Knowingly selling or dispensing any drug as a different drug or medical preparation.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 278 replaces IPC Section 276 for fraudulent substitution of medicines upon sale. Knowingly substituting one drug for another poses grave patient danger and now carries up to 1 year imprisonment.

title: Fouling water of public spring or reservoir
old_text: Corrupting or fouling the water of any public spring or reservoir so as to render it less fit for ordinary use.
new_text: Corrupting or fouling the water of any public spring, reservoir, or water source rendering it less fit for use.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to Rs. 500, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 279 replaces IPC Section 277 punishing pollution or fouling of public water sources. The term of imprisonment has been doubled to 6 months and fine increased to deter environmental and drinking water contamination.

title: Making atmosphere noxious to health
old_text: Vitiating the atmosphere in any place so as to make it noxious to the health of persons in general.
new_text: Vitiating the atmosphere in any locality so as to make it noxious to public health or residents.
punishment_old: Fine up to Rs. 500
punishment_new: Fine up to Rs. 1,000
explanation: BNS Section 280 replaces IPC Section 278 penalizing atmospheric air pollution that creates a health hazard. It penalizes polluting emissions and noxious air discharge affecting residents and passers-by.

title: Rash driving or riding on a public way
old_text: Driving or riding on any public way so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or cause hurt or injury.
new_text: Driving or riding any vehicle on a public way rashly or negligently endangering human life or likely to cause hurt.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 281 replaces IPC Section 279 for rash and negligent driving on public thoroughfares. It remains one of the most frequently invoked traffic offence sections in criminal litigation.

title: Rash navigation of vessel
old_text: Navigating any vessel rashly or negligently so as to endanger human life or cause hurt or injury.
new_text: Navigating any vessel rashly or negligently endangering human life or likely to cause hurt.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 10,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 282 replaces IPC Section 280 for reckless navigation of water vessels. The fine ceiling has been updated to Rs. 10,000 to deter reckless boating and maritime navigation.

title: Exhibition of false light, mark or buoy
old_text: Exhibiting any false light, mark or buoy, intending or knowing it is likely to mislead any navigator.
new_text: Exhibiting any false light, mark or buoy intending or knowing it is likely to mislead a navigator.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 7 years, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 283 replaces IPC Section 281 penalizing the deceptive display of navigation lights, buoys, or sea marks. Intentionally misleading mariners carries severe imprisonment up to 7 years due to the danger of shipwrecks.

title: Conveying person by water for hire in unsafe or overloaded vessel
old_text: Knowingly or negligently conveying any person by water for hire in an unsafe or overloaded vessel.
new_text: Knowingly or negligently conveying any passenger by water for hire in an overloaded or unsafe vessel.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 284 replaces IPC Section 282 penalizing ferry and boat operators who overload vessels or operate unseaworthy craft for commercial passenger transit. The fine limit has been elevated to Rs. 5,000.

title: Danger or obstruction in public way or line of navigation
old_text: Causing danger, obstruction or injury to any person in any public way or public line of navigation.
new_text: Causing danger, obstruction or injury to any person in a public way or public line of navigation.
punishment_old: Fine up to Rs. 200
punishment_new: Fine up to Rs. 5,000
explanation: BNS Section 285 replaces IPC Section 283 penalizing unauthorized road or waterway blockades. The maximum fine has been raised significantly from Rs. 200 to Rs. 5,000 to deter unlawful public encroachments.

title: Negligent conduct with respect to poisonous substance
old_text: Doing any rash or negligent act with a poisonous substance, or failing to guard against danger from it.
new_text: Rash or negligent handling of poisonous substance, or failing to take sufficient care to guard against danger.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 286 replaces IPC Section 284 penalizing reckless storage or handling of toxic and poisonous chemicals. The updated monetary fine ceiling strengthens accountability for industrial and chemical safety.

title: Negligent conduct with respect to fire or combustible matter
old_text: Acting rashly or negligently with fire or combustible matter so as to endanger human life or property.
new_text: Rash or negligent conduct with fire or combustible matter endangering life or property, or failing to guard against fire.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 2,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 287 replaces IPC Section 285 penalizing negligent handling of fire, inflammable liquids, or combustible materials. It addresses fire hazards endangering human safety and surrounding structures.

title: Negligent conduct with respect to explosive substance
old_text: Acting rashly or negligently with explosive substance so as to endanger human life or cause hurt.
new_text: Rash or negligent conduct with explosive substance endangering life or failing to guard against danger.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 288 replaces IPC Section 286 penalizing reckless handling, transit, or storage of explosives and fireworks. Penalties combine imprisonment up to 6 months with enhanced fine provisions.

title: Negligent conduct with respect to machinery
old_text: Acting rashly or negligently with machinery under one's care or failing to guard against danger to life.
new_text: Rash or negligent conduct with machinery or failing to take reasonable precautions against danger to human life.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 289 replaces IPC Section 287 governing factory and machinery maintenance negligence. Owners and operators must implement adequate safeguards to prevent worker and bystander injury.

title: Negligent conduct with respect to pulling down, repairing or constructing buildings
old_text: Negligently or knowingly omitting to take order with any building being pulled down or repaired, endangering human life.
new_text: Negligently omitting to take proper order in pulling down, repairing or constructing buildings endangering life.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 290 replaces IPC Section 288 governing construction, demolition, and building renovation hazards. It explicitly covers modern structural construction alongside pulling down or repairing dilapidated buildings.

title: Negligent conduct with respect to animal
old_text: Knowingly or negligently omitting to take order with an animal in possession so as to guard against danger.
new_text: Knowingly or negligently omitting to take precautions with any animal in one's possession endangering human life.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or both
explanation: BNS Section 291 replaces IPC Section 289 for negligent supervision of dangerous pets or animals. Owners who fail to restrain aggressive animals causing public danger face imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 5,000.

title: Continuance of nuisance after injunction to discontinue
old_text: Repeating or continuing a public nuisance after having been enjoined by a public servant not to repeat or continue it.
new_text: Continuing or repeating a public nuisance after receiving lawful injunction or order to discontinue it.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 292 replaces IPC Section 291 for persisting in a public nuisance despite formal magisterial injunctions. Disregarding lawful restraining orders elevates nuisance to a criminal misdemeanor punishable with up to 6 months imprisonment.

title: Sale, etc., of obscene books, etc.
old_text: Selling, distributing, printing or publicly exhibiting obscene books, pamphlets, representations or figures.
new_text: Selling, distributing, publishing, or circulating obscene books, writings, drawings, representations or figures.
punishment_old: First conviction: up to 2 years and fine up to Rs. 2,000; repeat: up to 5 years and fine up to Rs. 5,000
punishment_new: First conviction: up to 2 years and fine up to Rs. 5,000; repeat: up to 5 years and fine up to Rs. 10,000
explanation: BNS Section 293 replaces IPC Section 292 governing obscenity in published materials, books, and artistic representations. Fines for first and repeat convictions have been updated while preserving statutory exceptions for religious or genuine artistic bona fides.

title: Sale, etc., of obscene objects to child or young person
old_text: Selling, distributing or exhibiting obscene objects to any person under the age of twenty years.
new_text: Selling, distributing, circulating or offering obscene objects to any person under eighteen years of age.
punishment_old: First conviction: up to 3 years and fine up to Rs. 2,000; repeat: up to 7 years and fine up to Rs. 5,000
punishment_new: First conviction: up to 3 years and fine up to Rs. 5,000; repeat: up to 7 years and fine up to Rs. 10,000
explanation: BNS Section 294 replaces IPC Section 293 aligning the threshold age with the universal minority age of 18 years (previously 20 years under IPC). It prescribes strict punishment up to 3 years for first conviction and up to 7 years for repeats.

title: Obscene acts and songs
old_text: Doing any obscene act in a public place, or singing obscene songs or ballads in or near any public place.
new_text: Doing an obscene act in a public place, or singing or reciting obscene songs or words in public causing annoyance.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine, or both
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine, or both
explanation: BNS Section 295 replaces IPC Section 294 punishing obscene acts or indecent songs performed in public places causing annoyance. The essential requirement of proving public annoyance remains intact.

title: Keeping lottery office
old_text: Keeping any lottery office or publishing proposals regarding unapproved lotteries.
new_text: Keeping any lottery office or advertising unauthorized lotteries or gambling draws.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both; publishing proposals: fine up to Rs. 1,000
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both; publishing proposals: fine up to Rs. 5,000
explanation: BNS Section 296 replaces IPC Section 294A regulating unauthorized lottery offices and promotional lottery literature. State-authorized lotteries remain exempted while unauthorized commercial draws face up to 6 months imprisonment.

title: Punishment for public nuisance in cases not otherwise provided for
old_text: Punishment for public nuisance in any case not otherwise punishable by this Code.
new_text: General punishment for public nuisance in any case not specifically provided for under this Sanhita.
punishment_old: Fine up to Rs. 200
punishment_new: Fine up to Rs. 1,000
explanation: BNS Section 297 replaces IPC Section 290 as the omnibus sentencing clause for public nuisances not covered by specific penal provisions. The maximum fine is increased fivefold from Rs. 200 to Rs. 1,000.
